q-9909.name: Question 1
q-9909.worked_solution:
Let $u=1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $v=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{(-{sin}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

 Since ${sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{-1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{1-{cos}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that y=1+cos⁡xsin⁡x, find dydx.

a
−11−cos⁡x
b
11−cos⁡x
c
−11+cos⁡x
d
1sin2⁡x
e
−1sin2⁡x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let u=1+cos⁡x and v=sin⁡x. Then

dudx=−sin⁡xanddvdx=cos⁡x.

Using the quotient rule, we get

dydx=vdudx−udvdxv2=(−sin⁡x)(sin⁡x)−cos⁡x(1+cos⁡x)sin2⁡x=(−sin2⁡x−cos⁡x−cos2⁡x)sin2⁡x=−(sin2⁡x+cos2⁡x)−cos⁡xsin2⁡x. Since sin2⁡x+cos2⁡x=1, we have

dydx=−1−cos⁡xsin2⁡x=−(1+cos⁡x)1−cos2⁡x=−(1+cos⁡x)(1−cos⁡x)(1+cos⁡x)=−11−cos⁡x.

q-11969.name: Question 2
q-11969.worked_solution:
Let $u=-x$ and $v=9-2x.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =-1\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(9-2x)\cdot (-1)-(-x)\cdot (-2)}{{(9-2x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-9+2x-2x}{{(9-2x)}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{9}{{(9-2x)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-11969.html:
Question 2
?

Given that y=−x9−2x, find dydx.

a
−4x−9(9−2x)2
b
4x−9(9−2x)2
c
9(9−2x)2
d
−2x−9(9−2x)2
e
−9(9−2x)2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let u=−x and v=9−2x. Then

dudx=−1anddvdx=−2.

Using the quotient rule, we get

dydx=vdudx−udvdxv2=(9−2x)⋅(−1)−(−x)⋅(−2)(9−2x)2=−9+2x−2x(9−2x)2=−9(9−2x)2.

q-17921.name: Question 3
q-17921.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{′}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{′}}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x(\frac{1}{x})}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

If f(x)=cos⁡xln⁡x, find f′(x).

a
sin⁡xln⁡x−cos⁡xxln2⁡x
b
xsin⁡xln⁡x−cos⁡xxsin2⁡x
c
−xsin⁡xln⁡x−cos⁡xxln2⁡x
d
−sin⁡xln⁡x−sin⁡xxln2⁡x
e
xcos⁡xln⁡x−cos⁡xxln2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=cos⁡x and v(x)=ln⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(cos⁡x)′ln⁡x−(cos⁡x)(ln⁡x)′ln2⁡x=−sin⁡xln⁡x−cos⁡x(1x)ln2⁡x=−xsin⁡xln⁡x−cos⁡xxln2⁡x
